explanation: Equal values are adjacent in the sorted input. Append a value only when it differs from the most recently appended value.
spaceComplexity: O(u) output space for u distinct values; O(1) other space.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: After each input position, result contains exactly the distinct values seen so far, in sorted order. Sortedness places every repeat adjacent to its first occurrence, so a value equal to the last result entry is already represented. Any different value is a new distinct value and is appended. This invariant gives exactly one copy of every input value at completion.
walkthrough: Read [-4, -4, 2, 2, 2, 11]. Append the first -4 and skip its repeat. Append 2 and skip the next two 2s. Append 11. Return [-4, 2, 11].
edgeCases: Empty input returns an empty result.
An all-equal input keeps exactly one entry.
Negative values and integer extremes need only equality comparisons.
